---
title: "Project update"
subtitle: "How we ran the work: every task as a GitHub issue, opened, worked and closed in the open"
page-layout: full
---

```{ojs}
pm = FileAttachment("data/pm/issues.json").json()
```

```{ojs}
now = new Date(pm.generated_at)
```

```{ojs}
workstreamOrder = ["data", "analysis", "feature-engineering", "modelling", "submission", "process", "setup"]
```

```{ojs}
issues = pm.issues.map(d => ({
  ...d,
  created: new Date(d.created_at),
  closed: d.closed_at ? new Date(d.closed_at) : null,
  isClosed: d.state === "closed",
  ai: d.labels.includes("ai-assisted"),
  workstream: workstreamOrder.find(w => d.labels.includes(w)) ?? "other",
  daysOpen: ((d.closed_at ? new Date(d.closed_at) : new Date(pm.generated_at)) - new Date(d.created_at)) / 864e5
}))
```

```{ojs}
people = ({domain: ["Alan", "Bridget", "Cian", "Gerard"], range: ["#4e79a7", "#e15759", "#59a14f", "#f28e2b"], legend: true})
```

```{ojs}
kpi = {
  const closed = issues.filter(d => d.isClosed)
  const start = d3.min(issues, d => d.created)
  return {
    total: issues.length,
    closed: closed.length,
    open: issues.length - closed.length,
    rate: closed.length / issues.length,
    people: new Set(issues.map(d => d.owner)).size,
    days: Math.ceil((now - start) / 864e5),
    start,
    aiShare: issues.filter(d => d.ai).length / issues.length,
    medianDays: d3.median(closed, d => d.daysOpen),
    last7: closed.filter(d => now - d.closed < 7 * 864e5).length
  }
}
```

```{ojs}
html`<div class="hero-kpis">
  <div class="kpi-card"><div class="kpi-label">Issues raised</div><div class="kpi-value">${kpi.total}</div></div>
  <div class="kpi-card"><div class="kpi-label">Closed</div><div class="kpi-value">${kpi.closed} <small>(${Math.round(kpi.rate * 100)}%)</small></div></div>
  <div class="kpi-card"><div class="kpi-label">Median days to close</div><div class="kpi-value">${kpi.medianDays.toFixed(1)}</div></div>
  <div class="kpi-card"><div class="kpi-label">AI-assisted</div><div class="kpi-value">${Math.round(kpi.aiShare * 100)}%</div></div>
  <div class="kpi-card"><div class="kpi-label">Team / days</div><div class="kpi-value">${kpi.people} / ${kpi.days}</div></div>
</div>`
```

## Executive summary

```{ojs}
byOwner = d3.rollups(issues, v => ({raised: v.length, closed: v.filter(d => d.isClosed).length}), d => d.owner)
  .map(([owner, v]) => ({owner, ...v})).sort((a, b) => b.closed - a.closed)
```

```{ojs}
md`In **${kpi.days} days** since ${kpi.start.toLocaleDateString("en-GB", {day: "numeric", month: "long"})}, the team of
**${kpi.people}** raised **${kpi.total} issues** and closed **${kpi.closed}** (${Math.round(kpi.rate * 100)}%), ${kpi.last7} of them in
the last seven days. Every piece of work, from data fixes to model tests to this website, was raised as a GitHub issue,
worked, and closed with a note saying where it was done. That gives the judges a complete, time-stamped audit trail.
**${Math.round(kpi.aiShare * 100)}%** of issues are labelled *ai-assisted*, so the use of AI is recorded task by task.

Issues closed, by person: ${byOwner.map(d => `**${d.owner}** ${d.closed} of ${d.raised}`).join(" · ")}.`
```

*Data: the GitHub issues of [the repository](https://github.com/almac09/iaa-hackathon-2026/issues), refreshed on every
site build and daily.*

## Issues raised and closed over time

The gap between the two lines is the open work. A steep closed line means a delivery push.

```{ojs}
burnup = {
  const days = d3.timeDay.range(d3.timeDay.floor(kpi.start), d3.timeDay.offset(d3.timeDay.floor(now), 1))
  return days.flatMap(day => {
    const end = d3.timeDay.offset(day, 1)
    return [
      {day, series: "Raised", n: issues.filter(d => d.created < end).length},
      {day, series: "Closed", n: issues.filter(d => d.closed && d.closed < end).length}
    ]
  })
}
```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: 1000, height: 340, marginLeft: 50,
  color: {domain: ["Raised", "Closed"], range: ["#9c9c9c", "#2ca02c"], legend: true},
  x: {label: null, type: "utc"},
  y: {label: "Cumulative issues", grid: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.areaY(burnup.filter(d => d.series === "Closed"), {x: "day", y: "n", fill: "#2ca02c", fillOpacity: 0.15, curve: "step-after"}),
    Plot.line(burnup, {x: "day", y: "n", stroke: "series", strokeWidth: 2.5, curve: "step-after", tip: true}),
    Plot.ruleY([0])
  ]
})
```

## Gantt chart: every issue from opened to closed

Each bar is one issue, from the day it was raised to the day it was closed. Faded bars are still open and run to today.
Hover for the title.

```{ojs}
viewof ganttOwner = Inputs.select(["Everyone", "Alan", "Bridget", "Cian", "Gerard"], {label: "Person"})
```

```{ojs}
viewof ganttWorkstream = Inputs.select(["All workstreams", ...workstreamOrder, "other"], {label: "Workstream"})
```

```{ojs}
ganttRows = issues
  .filter(d => ganttOwner === "Everyone" || d.owner === ganttOwner)
  .filter(d => ganttWorkstream === "All workstreams" || d.workstream === ganttWorkstream)
  .map(d => ({...d, end: d.closed ?? now, label: `#${d.number} ${d.title.replace(/^\[AI-Assisted\]\s*/i, "").slice(0, 48)}`}))
```

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: 1000, height: Math.max(220, 40 + 11 * ganttRows.length), marginLeft: 330,
  color: people,
  x: {label: null, type: "utc", grid: true, domain: [d3.timeDay.floor(kpi.start), now]},
  y: {label: null, domain: ganttRows.map(d => d.label), tickSize: 0},
  style: {fontSize: "9px"},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(ganttRows, {
      x1: "created", x2: d => new Date(Math.max(+d.end, +d.created + 3 * 36e5)), y: "label", fill: "owner",
      fillOpacity: d => d.isClosed ? 0.95 : 0.35, inset: 0.5,
      title: d => `#${d.number} ${d.title}\n${d.owner} · ${d.workstream}\n${d.isClosed ? `closed after ${d.daysOpen.toFixed(1)} days` : "open"}`
    }),
    Plot.ruleX([now], {stroke: "#333", strokeDasharray: "3 3"})
  ]
})
```

## Who completed what

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: 1000, height: 300, marginLeft: 70,
  color: {legend: true, domain: [...workstreamOrder, "other"], scheme: "tableau10"},
  x: {label: "Issues closed", grid: true},
  y: {label: null, domain: byOwner.map(d => d.owner)},
  marks: [
    Plot.barX(issues.filter(d => d.isClosed), Plot.groupY({x: "count"}, {y: "owner", fill: "workstream", tip: true})),
    Plot.ruleX([0])
  ]
})
```

### Activity by day

Issues closed each day by each person: the rhythm of the project.

```{ojs}
Plot.plot({
  width: 1000, height: 220, marginLeft: 70, padding: 0.08,
  color: {scheme: "greens", legend: true, label: "Issues closed"},
  x: {label: null, type: "band", tickFormat: d => d3.utcFormat("%a %d")(new Date(d))},
  y: {label: null},
  marks: [
    Plot.cell(issues.filter(d => d.isClosed), Plot.group({fill: "count"}, {
      x: d => d3.utcDay.floor(d.closed).toISOString(), y: "owner", tip: true, inset: 1
    }))
  ]
})
```

## Recently closed

```{ojs}
Inputs.table(issues.filter(d => d.isClosed).sort((a, b) => b.closed - a.closed).slice(0, 15).map(d => ({
  issue: d.number, title: d.title, owner: d.owner, workstream: d.workstream, closed: d.closed, days: d.daysOpen
})), {
  format: {
    issue: n => html`<a href="https://github.com/${pm.repo}/issues/${n}" target="_blank">#${n}</a>`,

  },
  width: {title: 420}
})
```

## How we worked

* **One task, one issue.** Each issue has a short AI interaction log, the tasks, and a closing comment saying where the work
  was done (notebook cell, file or commit).
* **Labels by workstream** (data, analysis, feature engineering, modelling, submission, process, setup), plus
  *ai-assisted* for transparency.
* **Parent and sub-issues** for larger pieces of work, such as model explainability and this website.
* **Per-person branches, consolidated to `main`** under `contributors/`, with nobody else's branch rewritten.

```{ojs}
md`*Last refreshed ${d3.utcFormat("%d %B %Y, %H:%M UTC")(now)}. Owner = the issue's first assignee, or its author if
nobody is assigned.*`
```
